title: Rewrite rule item (frMatchRule)
$comment: The DynamoDB item shape the Lambda@Edge reads for a rewrite (origin-request). Modeled on ForwardRewriteRule/ForwardSettings from the source project's redirect-rule-types.ts. forwardSettings.origin is assigned straight to request.origin, so it mirrors the CloudFront origin structure from @types/aws-lambda.

pk.description: Host, e.g. www.example.com. DynamoDB partition key.

sk.description: REWRITE#<priority>, priority zero-padded to 5 digits; lower = higher priority; unique per host per type.

forwardSettings.$comment: At least one of origin / pathAndQS is meaningful; a rewrite that changes neither does nothing.

origin.$comment: Discriminated union: exactly one of s3 / custom, matching CloudFrontOrigin (with the extended custom protocol) in redirect-rule-types.ts / @types/aws-lambda.

pathAndQS.description: Rewritten path (and optional query string) the request is forwarded with: a path starting with "/", or a target starting with a capture reference ("$1/x").
pathAndQS.$comment: The edge assigns the path to request.uri, and CloudFront refuses a uri that does not start with "/" with a 502 (LambdaValidationError) on every request the rule matches. Whitespace, control characters and "#" are no more valid in a uri or the query string the edge sets from it ("Restrictions on all edge functions"). A target starting with `$n` is a template whose leading segment only exists once the edge substitutes it, so the edge adds the "/" itself when the capture lacks one. Empty stays allowed: the edge reads it as "keep the incoming path".

useIncomingQueryString.description: Whether the request's own query string is forwarded. Absent means yes — only an explicit false drops it. A query string written into pathAndQS wins over either.
useIncomingQueryString.$comment: Absent is deliberately not an opt-out: forwarding is what this field has always done when omitted, both here and in the upstream snippet, so rules written by hand keep behaving the same. See infra/lambda/README.md#the-query-string-on-a-rewrite.

disabled.$comment: Optional; absent means enabled. The Lambda@Edge filters out rules where disabled=true (RulesService.loadRules), so a toggle takes effect within the edge cache TTL (~1 min). The console writes it through PATCH.

originPath.$comment:
Empty, or starting with "/" and not ending with one: "/v1", not "v1" or "/v1/".

CloudFront validates the origin the edge returns on every request, and any origin field outside its limits turns each request the rule matches into a 502 (LambdaValidationError). The limits in s3Origin and customOrigin are CloudFront's, from the origin fields of the Lambda@Edge request event. Header names CloudFront refuses to set are checked in console/api/src/lib/assert-origin-headers.ts instead, because that check is case-insensitive and draft-07 patterns have no flag for it.

cloudFrontHeaders.$comment: CloudFrontHeaders: lower-cased header name -> array of { key?, value }.

domainName.$comment: The bucket's DNS name, e.g. my-bucket.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com: all lowercase, at most 128 characters, no scheme or path.

region.$comment: Required by the type when authMethod is origin-access-identity; must be absent when authMethod is none.

domainName.$comment: A DNS name like api.example.com: no scheme, port, path, or colon, and not an IP address.

keepaliveTimeout.$comment: The event reference allows up to 120, but CloudFront's default keep-alive quota is 60, and a value above an account's quota may be refused at request time.

port.$comment: CloudFront connects to 80, 443, or 1024-65535 only. Spelled as a range minus its gaps rather than an anyOf of the allowed values, so the generated TypeScript type stays `number`.

readTimeout.$comment: 120 is CloudFront's default quota; an account with a raised quota would need this raised too.
